Order defines the 12-bit GPU material ID. Worldgen and world.h assume it — new materials are appended at the end, reordering is disabled, and deleting anything but the last entry will shift every later ID.

schema notes (from reactions.json)
file order matters: rules for the same self are tried top-down, at most one fires per cell per tick. chance is ‰ per 30 Hz tick, and may be fractional — 1‰ is a ~33 s mean wait, 0.01‰ is ~55 min, and the floor is 0.0005‰.

Edits are a LAYER over worldgen, not a saved world. The engine applies assets/worldedits/*.svedit after generating a chunk and on every stream-in, so an edit survives flying away and composes with any seed. Pick the layer in the map page's edits selector (tuning.json world.editLayer) to make the game load it.
How edits reach the game: R in-game hot-reloads items alongside materials and glyphs — no rebuild. Regenerating the art (python scripts/gen_sword_item.py) overwrites the sidecar, so tune here or there, not both.
